strings.d1.s0.name: Giza Pyramids
strings.d1.s0.tips: Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure; cool and empty at the 07:00 opening. Entering the Great Pyramid costs an extra 1,500 EGP (narrow tunnel). Haggle camel rides at 200-300 EGP; pay by card.
strings.d1.s1.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
strings.d1.s1.tips: Included in the pyramid ticket. Approach from the Valley Temple; morning light hits the face.
strings.d1.s2.name: Panorama Point Giza
strings.d1.s2.tips: A desert viewpoint that takes in all three pyramids at once: the classic photo.
strings.d1.s3.name: Khufu's Restaurant Giza
strings.d1.s3.tips: Modern Egyptian cooking with pyramid views. Book ahead; 9 Pyramids Lounge is the alternative.
strings.d1.s4.name: Giza Sound and Light Show
strings.d1.s4.tips: A light and sound show in front of the Sphinx. Nights are cool; buy tickets in advance.
strings.d1.b0.name: 9 Pyramids Lounge
strings.d1.b0.tips: Lunch in the desert with pyramid views; go here if Khufu's is full.
strings.d1.b1.name: Giza Camel Tour
strings.d1.b1.tips: 30 minutes by camel in the desert; fix the price beforehand.
strings.d2.s0.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: The huge museum that opened in 2025: Tutankhamun's complete treasure (5,000 pieces) and Khufu's solar boat. Book a timed ticket online (~1,450 EGP); allow 3-4 hours and take a morning slot.
strings.d2.s1.name: GEM Food Court
strings.d2.s1.tips: Eating area inside the museum, with pyramid views.
strings.d2.s2.name: Grand Egyptian Museum Garden and Obelisk
strings.d2.s2.tips: The hanging obelisk and the outer courtyard; photograph them against the pyramid skyline.
strings.d2.s3.name: Koshary Abou Tarek
strings.d2.s3.tips: Cairo's most famous koshary (rice, lentils and pasta) since the 1950s. Downtown, four floors, 80 EGP.
strings.d2.b0.name: Zooba Downtown
strings.d2.b0.tips: Modern Egyptian street food: ta'meya and hawawshi.
strings.d2.b1.name: Egyptian Museum Tahrir
strings.d2.b1.tips: The old museum, with the mummies and artefacts that were not moved to the GEM.
strings.d3.s0.name: Citadel of Saladin & Muhammad Ali Mosque
strings.d3.s0.tips: The citadel and the alabaster mosque; the terrace has views over Cairo and the pyramids.
strings.d3.s1.name: Sultan Hassan Mosque
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Mamluk masterpiece, with a huge courtyard and a sense of calm.
strings.d3.s2.name: Al-Muizz Street
strings.d3.s2.tips: A Fatimid street of mosques, sabils (public fountains) and the Beit el-Suhaymi house, lit up at night.
strings.d3.s3.name: Naguib Mahfouz Cafe
strings.d3.s3.tips: Run by Oberoi inside Khan el-Khalili. Try the molokhia (jute leaf stew) and mint tea; air-conditioned.
strings.d3.s4.name: Khan el-Khalili
strings.d3.s4.tips: A 14th-century bazaar selling copper, spices and papyrus. Bargain down to a third of the first price; El Fishawy cafe is open 24 hours.
strings.d3.b0.name: El Fishawy Cafe
strings.d3.b0.tips: A mirrored cafe since 1773; mint tea and shisha.
strings.d3.b1.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
strings.d3.b1.tips: A mosque-university since 970; visit instead of Sultan Hassan.
strings.d4.s0.name: Hanging Church
strings.d4.s0.tips: A 3rd-century church built over a Roman fortress, in Coptic Cairo. Take the metro to Mar Girgis.
strings.d4.s1.name: Coptic Museum
strings.d4.s1.tips: Coptic art and the Nag Hammadi texts.
strings.d4.s2.name: Ben Ezra Synagogue
strings.d4.s2.tips: Said to be where Moses was found; home of the Cairo Geniza.
strings.d4.s3.name: Abou El Sid Zamalek
strings.d4.s3.tips: Egyptian cooking in 1920s decor in Zamalek: stuffed pigeon and molokhia.
strings.d4.s4.name: Nile Felucca Ride
strings.d4.s4.tips: One hour on a sailing felucca from Zamalek. Go at sunset and haggle per boat.
strings.d4.b0.name: Sequoia Zamalek
strings.d4.b0.tips: A riverside terrace on the Nile; shisha and meze, instead of the felucca.
strings.d4.b1.name: Cairo Tower
strings.d4.b1.tips: A 187 m tower in Zamalek with city views.
strings.d5.s0.name: Saqqara Step Pyramid
strings.d5.s0.tips: The world's oldest pyramid (Djoser). The Serapeum's underground bull sarcophagi need an extra ticket; cooler in the morning.
strings.d5.s1.name: Dahshur Red Pyramid
strings.d5.s1.tips: Entry into the Red Pyramid is included (steep tunnel). Next to the Bent Pyramid, with few tourists.
strings.d5.s2.name: Memphis Open Air Museum
strings.d5.s2.tips: The ancient capital, with a colossal statue of Ramses II and an alabaster sphinx.
strings.d5.s3.name: Saqqara Country Club Lunch
strings.d5.s3.tips: A farm restaurant among palm trees: grills and Egyptian bread.
strings.d5.s4.name: Saqqara Carpet School
strings.d5.s4.tips: A hand-woven carpet workshop; no pressure to buy, just watch.
strings.d5.b0.name: Abou Shakra Giza
strings.d5.b0.tips: A kebab classic; stop on the way back.
strings.d5.b1.name: Bent Pyramid Dahshur
strings.d5.b1.tips: Inside the Bent Pyramid; go instead of the Red Pyramid.
strings.d6.s0.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
strings.d6.s0.tips: 2.5 hours by train from Cairo; a modern library and museums in a disc-shaped building.
strings.d6.s1.name: Qaitbay Citadel
strings.d6.s1.tips: A 15th-century fortress on the site of the ancient lighthouse, with Mediterranean views.
strings.d6.s2.name: Fish Market Restaurant Alexandria
strings.d6.s2.tips: Fish on the Corniche: pick yours from the counter, with Mediterranean views.
strings.d6.s3.name: Kom El Shoqafa Catacombs
strings.d6.s3.tips: Roman-era underground tombs, mixing Egyptian and Greek styles.
strings.d6.s4.name: Alexandria Corniche
strings.d6.s4.tips: Walk the seafront boulevard and take the tram to Montaza; the return train is at 18:00.
strings.d6.b0.name: Mohamed Ahmed Foul Alexandria
strings.d6.b0.tips: Alexandria's classic for ful and falafel.
strings.d6.b1.name: Pompey's Pillar
strings.d6.b1.tips: A Roman column; go instead of the catacombs.
strings.d7.s0.name: Gezira Island Zamalek Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: The island district: ivy-covered embassy streets and the Nile.
strings.d7.s1.name: Aisha Fahmy Palace
strings.d7.s1.tips: An Art Nouveau palace and gallery in Zamalek.
strings.d7.s2.name: Ovio Zamalek
strings.d7.s2.tips: Zamalek's breakfast and brunch cafe; a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s3.name: Zamalek Nile Bank Last Tea
strings.d7.s3.tips: A last tea at a cafe with Nile views; the airport is 45 minutes away.
strings.d7.b0.name: Cairo Kitchen Zamalek
strings.d7.b0.tips: Home cooking; go instead of Ovio.
strings.d7.b1.name: Museum of Islamic Art Cairo
strings.d7.b1.tips: One of the world's best collections of Islamic art; go instead of the Zamalek plan.
strings.note0: Uber and Careem are safe and cheap. Taxis don't use meters, so agree the fare beforehand. Metro Line 1 goes to Coptic Cairo (Mar Girgis). Traffic to Giza takes 1 hour.
strings.note1: October to April is ideal (20-28°C). December and January mornings are 10°C and evenings are cool. During Ramadan, restaurants are closed in the daytime.
strings.note2: Monument entry is by card only in 2026, no cash. Book GEM timed tickets online; entering the Great Pyramid at Giza costs 1,500 EGP.
strings.note3: Koshary costs 50-80 EGP, ful and ta'meya 30, restaurants 300-600. Tip (baksheesh) 20-50 EGP everywhere, 10% in restaurants.
strings.note4: There are no 'free' photo or camel offers at the pyramids: say 'la shukran' (no thank you) and keep walking. Women will be more comfortable with shoulders and knees covered.
strings.note5: Take your shoes off and wear a headscarf in mosques; don't visit during Friday midday prayer.
